**Primært kirurgisk indgreb** (primary surgical intervention) is a procedural classification used in Danish healthcare quality monitoring, specifically serving as the definitional foundation for calculating Indicator 6 in the DANIBD 2024 report [^src1]. Indicator 6 tracks the rate of re-operations within 30 days following a primary surgical intervention, making the precise definition of what constitutes a "primary" procedure critical for evaluating surgical quality and regional performance [^src1].

A surgical intervention is classified as primary if it involves specific procedure codes—such as KJFB*, KJFC*, KJFF*, KJFG (excluding 40H/K, 41A, 50A, and 60), KJFH*, KJFW*, KJGB*, and specific KJFA codes—and, crucially, if there has been no prior surgical intervention with corresponding codes within the preceding 30 days [^src1]. This 30-day lookback period ensures that subsequent or related procedures are correctly categorized as re-operations rather than primary interventions, directly impacting the accuracy of the quality metrics reported in the registry [^src1].

The concept is central to the methodological framework of the DANIBD 2024 report, which analyzes surgical quality data, including the revision of procedure codes and the variation in re-operation rates across different regions and departments [^src1]. While the report highlights progress in other areas, such as fulfilling the development goal for Indicator 5 (f-calprotectin measurement), it also underscores challenges related to Indicator 6, noting a failure to meet the national target and significant regional disparities in re-operation rates following these primary interventions [^src1].
